newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Sasol, Phillips sign Qatar gas memo.
newsitem.headline: Sasol, Phillips sign Qatar gas memo.

text.p: South African fuel and chemicals firm Sasol Ltd said on Wednesday that it had signed a memorandum of understanding with Qatar General Petroleum Corp (QGPC) and Phillips Petroleum Corp to build a gas-to-liquids plant at Ras Laffan in the tiny Gulf country.
The joint-venture will be 51 percent owned by QGPC, 34 percent owned by Sasol and Phillips will take the remaining 15 percent.
A six month feasibilty study will now begin on the viability of the proposed plant and, if it recommends a go-ahead, work will begin with the aim of completing construction during 2002.

"This pioneering project will confirm Sasol's leadership in the conversion of gas to fuels and chemicals. It enables Sasol to break new ground in its globalisation drive," said Pat Davies, Sasol group general manager.
The plant will use Sasol's slurry phase distillate process technology to convert natural gas into about 20,000 barrels per day of naphtha and other distillate fuels.
Sasol orginally announced it was in talks on the plant in March.
